questions.question: What are reactants?
choices: Only the gases released during heating
Substances produced by a reaction only
All containers used during an experiment
Substances present before and consumed in a reaction

questions.question: What are products?
choices: The equipment used to start a reaction
Substances formed by a chemical reaction
The original chemicals before mixing
Only chemicals that remain unchanged

questions.question: Which principle requires equal numbers of each kind of atom on both sides of a balanced equation?
choices: Conservation of atoms
Equal volume
Constant color
Constant temperature

questions.question: What does a coefficient in a chemical equation change?
choices: The identity of an element
The subscripts within one compound formula
The number of protons in an atom
The relative number of particles or moles represented

questions.question: What is a precipitate?
choices: A gas produced only by boiling
A liquid produced only by melting
An insoluble solid formed from a solution during a reaction
A solvent that contains no dissolved material

questions.question: What is an exothermic reaction?
choices: A reaction that absorbs net energy from its surroundings
A reaction that creates new atoms from energy in an ordinary beaker
A reaction that cannot involve gases
A reaction that transfers net energy to its surroundings

questions.question: What is a catalyst?
choices: A substance that must become the final product
A substance that speeds a reaction without being consumed overall
A substance that replaces every reactant
A substance that changes atom counts in an equation

questions.question: Why is rusting classified as a chemical change?
choices: The iron changes location
The iron is only bent into a new shape
New substances form as iron reacts with its surroundings
The sample's mass must always decrease

questions.question: Why must a reaction equation be balanced using coefficients rather than changing formulas?
choices: Changing a formula can change the substance being represented
Formulas can never include numbers
Coefficients change the identity of each element
Balancing requires adding protons to the reactants

questions.question: Why can a gas-producing reaction appear to lose mass in an open container?
choices: The reaction destroys some of its atoms
Gas has no mass
Some products leave the measured system
Every open container creates new neutrons

questions.question: How does a closed system help demonstrate mass conservation in an ordinary reaction?
choices: It prevents every chemical change
It requires equal volumes of all reactants
It makes gases weigh more than liquids
It retains the matter involved in the reaction

questions.question: Why is a color change evidence to investigate rather than proof of a reaction by itself?
choices: Mixing or other physical processes can also change appearance
Color can never change during a reaction
A chemical reaction must always make a white product
Color determines the number of atoms in every sample

questions.question: How does increasing temperature often speed a reaction?
choices: The atoms gain extra protons in ordinary conditions
Particles collide more frequently or with greater energy
Every catalyst is used up faster
Reactants no longer need to meet

questions.question: Why can crushing a solid reactant speed its reaction with a liquid?
choices: It increases exposed surface area
It changes the solid into a new element
It lowers the number of atoms in the sample
It eliminates contact with the liquid

questions.question: What happens to atoms in an ordinary chemical reaction?
choices: They all become different elements
They disappear when bonds break
They are rearranged into new combinations
They remain in the same molecular arrangements

questions.question: What coefficients balance H₂ + O₂ → H₂O using the smallest whole numbers?
A sealed container initially holds 12 g of one reactant and 8 g of another, with no other material. No matter enters or leaves. What is the total mass inside after the reaction?
choices: 4 g

questions.question: A student changes H₂O to H₂O₂ to balance an equation. What is the main problem?
choices: The student has changed the chemical identity of the product
The total number of oxygen atoms cannot change in a formula
The student has used a coefficient
The student has removed all hydrogen atoms

questions.question: A solution forms bubbles when chemicals are mixed. Which test best helps distinguish a chemical reaction from ordinary boiling?
choices: Compare the liquid level without identifying the gas
Check whether the liquid is transparent
Identify a newly produced gas under conditions that do not cause boiling
Assume every bubble proves a reaction

questions.question: Two trials use equal amounts of a solid, but one uses powder and one uses a single chunk. All other conditions match. Why might the powder react faster?
choices: It contains more protons per atom
It offers more surface area for contact
Its atoms have become a different element
Its chemical formula changes when ground
